title: ESCCseeker: machine learning on blood DNA methylation stratifies esophageal cancer risk
summary: In a two-stage multicenter study in China, machine learning combined eight differentially methylated positions from peripheral blood mononuclear cells with age, gender, SCC-Ag and CYFRA21-1 into the ESCCseeker model (AUC 0.987 training, 0.966 test, 0.943 verification). In a prospective multicenter cohort, a predefined cutoff split individuals into low- and high-risk groups; restricting endoscopy to the high-risk group cut the endoscopies needed from 25.02 to 4.78 (83% avoided) while keeping more than 90% detection sensitivity. The trial is registered as ChiCTR2500095967; clinical outcomes beyond triage were not reported in the abstract.
ai_technology: Machine-learning model integrating DNA methylation markers with age, sex and serum markers
organization: Second Hospital of Shandong University; Qilu Hospital of Shandong University

evidence.tested: Test and verification cohorts plus a prospective multicenter cohort with a predefined cutoff.
evidence.unknown: Effect on screening outcomes and generalization beyond the studied centers; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning combined methylation and clinical markers into the risk model.
